title: The Character I Almost Overlooked: Ebed-Melech
paragraphs:
The Character I Almost Overlooked: Ebed-Melech
Lesson: A foreigner who rescued Jeremiah.
They threw Jeremiah into a pit.

Not a prison cell.
Not a dark room.
A pit.
The Bible says there was no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into it.
And while God’s prophet was slowly dying beneath the city…
most people stayed silent.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The man who moved was not a priest.
Not a prophet.
Not a king.
He was Ebed-Melech—a foreigner, an Ethiopian eunuch, a servant in the king’s house.
The overlooked man saw what the powerful ignored.
God saw it.

Jeremiah 38:9 says Ebed-Melech went to the king and said,
“These men have done evil in all that they did to Jeremiah the prophet.”
Read that again.
He called evil evil when silence would have been safer.

You knew there are moments when God does not ask you to be famous.
He asks you to be faithful.
Ebed-Melech took men, ropes, and old rags, and he pulled Jeremiah out of the pit.
Old rags.
Even his mercy was careful.

He didn’t just rescue Jeremiah.
He protected him from further wounds.
And God did not forget.

In Jeremiah 39:18, the Lord said to Ebed-Melech:
“I will surely save you… because you have put your trust in Me.”
That is the Gospel shadow.

A man goes down into a pit.
A rescuer comes from an unexpected place.
Judgment is coming.
But trust in God becomes the dividing line between death and deliverance.
And then Jesus comes.

Not merely to pull prophets from mud—
but to pull sinners from death.
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” — Luke 19:10

You were not just stuck.
You were sinking.

Sin was the pit.
Pride was the mud.
Silence was killing you.
But Christ came down.

He bore the cross.
He took the judgment.
He rose again.

Salvation is not earned by heroic acts.
It is received by grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.” — Ephesians 2:8–9
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
So here is the question:
Will you keep walking past the pit…
or will you become the kind of person God can trust in a collapsing generation?

Repent.
Believe in Jesus.
Obey when it costs you.
Because heaven remembers the overlooked faithful.
